# package client

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/client"
```

Package client is the DNP3 master (IEEE 1815-2012).

A [Client](#type-client) talks to one outstation. [Dial](#func-dial) connects and runs the startup sequence (with secure authentication and an update key, the session key change first; then clearing DEVICE\_RESTART, disabling and enabling unsolicited responses and an integrity poll, as [WithStartup](#func-withstartup) says); [New](#func-new) and [Client.Connect](#func-client-connect) do the same in two steps. Requests are methods that block until the outstation answered or the context ended: [Client.IntegrityPoll](#func-client-integritypoll), [Client.EventPoll](#func-client-eventpoll), [Client.Read](#func-client-read), [Client.Operate](#func-client-operate), [Client.SyncTime](#func-client-synctime), [Client.ColdRestart](#func-client-coldrestart), [Client.Broadcast](#func-client-broadcast), [Client.ReadAttributeSet](#func-client-readattributeset), the file transfer methods and more. Unsolicited responses and the measurements of every response go to the [Handler](#type-handler) of [WithHandler](#func-withhandler).

Transports: TCP (the default, port 20000), TLS ([WithTLS](#func-withtls)), UDP ([UDP](#func-udp) with [WithStream](#func-withstream)), any byte stream such as a serial port ([WithStream](#func-withstream)), and the dual end point, where the outstation establishes the connection ([Accept](#func-accept)).

For a long-running master: [WithReconnect](#func-withreconnect) re-establishes a lost channel with backoff, [WithRetry](#func-withretry) repeats the requests that are safe to repeat, [WithPoll](#func-withpoll) runs periodic polls, [WithLogger](#func-withlogger) and [WithMetrics](#func-withmetrics) report what happens. Secure Authentication version 5 is [WithSecureAuthentication](#func-withsecureauthentication), with [WithKeyChangeInterval](#func-withkeychangeinterval) and [WithAggressiveMode](#func-withaggressivemode).

Errors match the sentinels of the root package with errors.Is; see ERRORS.md. API.md lists the whole API.

## Constants

```go
const DefaultKeyChangeCount = 1000
```

DefaultKeyChangeCount is the default session key change count: the number of authentication messages, sent or received, after which the session keys are changed (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.6.1.4.4).

```go
const DefaultPort = 20000
```

DefaultPort is the registered DNP3 port, also used for TLS.

```go
const MaxKeyChangeCount = 1 << 31
```

MaxKeyChangeCount is the largest session key change count: half the range of the key change sequence number (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.6.1.4.4).

## Types

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {

	// the last unsolicited response, to recognise repeats
	// integrity is when the last integrity poll completed, so that an
	// automatic one queued before it is not run as well.

	// started is closed when the startup sequence of the current channel
	// has ended: automatic tasks wait for it.

	// auth is the secure authentication state of the current channel and
	// counters the security statistics.

	// rekey asks the key change loop for a key change now.

	// turn admits one transaction at a time; waiting counts the requests
	// queued for it.

	// needTime is the NEED_TIME indication of the outstation's latest
	// response.

}
```

Client is a DNP3 master for one outstation. Create it with [New](#func-new) or [Dial](#func-dial). It is safe for concurrent use; requests are executed one at a time, in the order they are made, as DNP3 requires.

#### func (Client) ActivateConfig

```go
func (c *Client) ActivateConfig(ctx context.Context, headers ...app.Header) ([]app.ActivateConfigStatus, error)
```

ActivateConfig sends ACTIVATE\_CONFIG (function code 31) with the given headers, which name the configurations to activate: file specifications (g70v8), for example

	c.ActivateConfig(ctx, app.FreeFormat(app.G70V8, app.FileSpecification{Name: "config.xml"}))

or octet strings (g110). It returns the status of requested operation of every g91v1 object of the response, usually one. A response without g91v1, or with one that is not a valid status, fails with dnp3.ErrProtocol; an outstation that refuses the request fails it with a \*dnp3.IINError. The request is never repeated (WithRetry).

#### func (Client) Broadcast

```go
func (c *Client) Broadcast(ctx context.Context, dest link.Address, fc app.FunctionCode, headers ...app.Header) error
```

Broadcast sends a request to every outstation on the channel, at the broadcast address dest: link.BroadcastNoConfirm (0xFFFD), link.BroadcastConfirm (0xFFFE, confirmation mandatory) or link.BroadcastOptionalConfirm (0xFFFF, confirmation optional). Nobody answers; each outstation executes the request and sets IIN1.0 BROADCAST in its next response. Requests that need an answer (READ, SELECT, OPERATE, the file and authentication functions) cannot be broadcast.


Close closes the channel, stops reconnecting and the automatic tasks, and fails pending requests with dnp3.ErrClosed. It waits for the client's goroutines, the handler included, to finish.

#### func (Client) Connect

```go
func (c *Client) Connect(ctx context.Context) error
```

Connect establishes the channel and runs the startup sequence of WithStartup (with secure authentication and an update key, the session key change first). When the sequence fails, the channel is closed and the error returned. It fails with dnp3.ErrBusy when the client is connected or connecting. With WithReconnect it needs to succeed only once: a lost channel is re-established by the client, and kept when only the startup sequence of the new one failed.

### type Handler

```go
type Handler interface {
	HandleMeasurements(info ResponseInfo, ms []Measurement)
}
```

Handler receives measurements. It is called for every fragment of every response and unsolicited response, in the order they arrived, on a goroutine of the client's own: a slow handler does not delay the protocol, and a handler may issue requests.

### type Measurement

```go
type Measurement struct {
	// GV is the object the value was sent as, for example app.G30V5.
	GV app.GroupVariation
	// Index is the point index.
	Index uint32
	// Value is one of the point value types of package app: app.Binary,
	// app.DoubleBitBinary, app.BinaryCommandEvent, app.Counter,
	// app.Analog, app.AnalogDeadband, app.AnalogCommandEvent,
	// app.AbsoluteTime (g50v4, a time and interval), app.BCD,

	// Event is set for objects of an event group.

}
```

Measurement is one point value or event of a response: indexed data of a point, sent with its index. Objects without an index that describe the device or a procedure, such as the time and date of time synchronization (g50v1..g50v3), are not measurements; OBJECTS.md marks the objects that are.

#### func WithAddresses

```go
func WithAddresses(local, remote link.Address) Option
```

WithAddresses sets the link addresses of the master (local) and of the outstation (remote). The defaults are 1 and 10.

#### func WithAggressiveMode

```go
func WithAggressiveMode(fcs ...app.FunctionCode) Option
```

WithAggressiveMode sends the requests with the function codes fcs (secauth.DefaultCritical when none are given) in Secure Authentication aggressive mode (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.5.3.3, A.45.3 and A.45.9): with a MAC in the request itself, so that the outstation executes it without a challenge. The MAC covers the last challenge received and the whole request up to the MAC value (Table A-9). Aggressive mode is used only once a challenge was answered successfully since the last session key change, so the first critical request after each key change is still challenged; after a refused aggressive mode request the next one is sent normally, and an outstation that answers error 4 (aggressive mode not supported) is not sent aggressive mode again on that connection. New refuses it without WithSecureAuthentication.

#### func WithAutoClearRestart

```go
func WithAutoClearRestart(enabled bool) Option
```

WithAutoClearRestart controls whether the client clears IIN1.7 (DEVICE\_RESTART) when the outstation reports it. It is on by default.

#### func WithAutoEventPoll

```go
func WithAutoEventPoll(enabled bool) Option
```

WithAutoEventPoll makes the client poll the classes the outstation reports events for (IIN1.1..1.3).

#### func WithAutoIntegrity

```go
func WithAutoIntegrity(enabled bool) Option
```

WithAutoIntegrity controls whether the client runs an integrity poll when the outstation reports a restart or an event buffer overflow. It is on by default.

#### func WithChallengeMACs

```go
func WithChallengeMACs(algs ...app.MACAlgorithm) Option
```

WithChallengeMACs limits the MAC algorithms an outstation's challenge may ask for. The challenge (g120v1, IEEE 1815-2012 A.45.1) names the algorithm of the reply and of aggressive mode requests; a challenge asking for another one fails the request with dnp3.ErrAuthentication. By default every algorithm package secauth computes is accepted except the obsolete HMAC-SHA-1 truncated to 4 octets and, over TCP/IP or UDP/IP (the built-in dialer, or a stream whose remote address is a TCP or UDP address), the truncations to 8 octets, which clauses 7.6.1.1.1 and 7.6.1.1.2 allow on serial links only; this option can allow them. The algorithm of secauth.User is the one the session key change and the outstation's key status use; it need not be in the list.

#### func WithKeyChangeCount

```go
func WithKeyChangeCount(n uint32) Option
```

WithKeyChangeCount sets the session key change count (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.6.1.4.4): with an update key, the session keys are also changed once n authentication messages were sent or received since the last change (challenges and errors received, replies and aggressive mode requests sent). The default is DefaultKeyChangeCount (1000); n ranges from 1 to MaxKeyChangeCount.

#### func WithKeyChangeInterval

```go
func WithKeyChangeInterval(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithKeyChangeInterval sets how often the session keys are changed while connected, with an update key (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.6.1.4.3). The default is 15 minutes. 0 disables the interval: the keys are then changed only after the key change count (WithKeyChangeCount), as the clause allows for devices that communicate infrequently. A negative interval is refused.

#### func WithSecureAuthentication

```go
func WithSecureAuthentication(u secauth.User) Option
```

WithSecureAuthentication enables Secure Authentication version 5: the client answers the outstation's challenges of critical requests. With an update key in u it first runs the session key change on every connection, and again at the key change interval; with only a session key it uses that key directly. A user number of 0, which IEEE 1815-2012 reserves for an unknown user, is taken as 1, the default user. Without this option a challenge fails the request with dnp3.ErrAuthentication.

#### func WithSolicitedConfirm

```go
func WithSolicitedConfirm(enabled bool) Option
```

WithSolicitedConfirm controls whether the client confirms a solicited response that asks for confirmation (CON). It is on by default, as IEEE 1815-2012 requires. It is a test and diagnostic option, to see what an outstation does without the confirmation: it keeps the events it sent (the next poll gets them again) and sends no further fragment of a multi-fragment response, so such a response ends in dnp3.ErrTimeout. Unsolicited responses are still confirmed; see WithUnsolicitedConfirm.

```go
func WithStartup(s Startup) Option
```

WithStartup sets what the client does each time the channel is established.


WithStateHandler sets a function called on every change of the channel state, with the error that caused it (nil when the application closed the client).

#### func WithUnsolicitedConfirm

```go
func WithUnsolicitedConfirm(enabled bool) Option
```

WithUnsolicitedConfirm controls whether the client confirms an unsolicited response that asks for confirmation (CON). It is on by default, as IEEE 1815-2012 requires. It is a test and diagnostic option, to see the outstation repeat an unconfirmed unsolicited response: the client passes the events of a repeat to the Handler only once. An outstation may answer no request until its null unsolicited response at startup is confirmed.

### type Startup

```go
type Startup struct {
	// DisableUnsolicited sends DISABLE_UNSOLICITED for classes 1..3 first.
	DisableUnsolicited bool
	// Integrity runs an integrity poll. When the outstation has asked for
	// the time (NEED_TIME) and WithTimeSync is set, the time is
	// synchronized first, so that the poll's events carry synchronized time.
	Integrity bool
	// EnableUnsolicited sends ENABLE_UNSOLICITED for these classes last.
	EnableUnsolicited []int
}
```

Startup configures what the client does each time the channel is established, before Connect returns. A step the outstation rejects (an IINError, such as IIN2.0 from an outstation without unsolicited responses) is logged and the sequence goes on; a step without a valid response fails it.

### type StreamOpener

```go
type StreamOpener func(ctx context.Context) (stream io.ReadWriteCloser, remote net.Addr, err error)
```

StreamOpener opens a byte stream that is not a TCP connection, for example a serial port. remote names the stream in logs and metrics and may be nil.

#### func Accept

```go
func Accept(l net.Listener) StreamOpener
```

Accept returns a StreamOpener for an outstation that establishes the connection (the dual end point of IEEE 1815-2012): it waits for the outstation to connect on l. Use it with WithStream; with WithReconnect the client waits for the next connection when one ends. The client does not close l. For TLS, give a listener of tls.NewListener: the master is the TLS server of such a connection.

	l, _ := net.Listen("tcp", ":20000")
	c, err := client.New("outstation", client.WithStream(client.Accept(l)))

#### func UDP

```go
func UDP(addr string) StreamOpener
```

UDP returns a StreamOpener for DNP3 over UDP (port 20000 by convention): every link frame travels in a datagram to addr ("host:port"). Use it with WithStream:

	c, err := client.New(addr, client.WithStream(client.UDP(addr)))

### type TimeSync

```go
type TimeSync uint8
```

TimeSync selects the time synchronization procedure.

```go
const (
	// TimeSyncNone disables automatic time synchronization.
	TimeSyncNone TimeSync = iota
	// TimeSyncLAN is the LAN procedure: RECORD_CURRENT_TIME, then a
	// WRITE of the time of that request (g50v3).
	TimeSyncLAN
	// TimeSyncNonLAN is the serial procedure: DELAY_MEASURE, then a WRITE
	// of the current time corrected by the measured delay (g50v1).
	TimeSyncNonLAN
)
```

Time synchronization procedures (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 5.2).
